item.title: What Happens When Patients Ask AI First? - MedCity News
item.description: Patients who better understand their conditions often ask more informed questions and participate more actively in shared decision-making. But fluency is not the same as reliability.

item.title: NYU Stern Report Urges Regulation of Private Equity in Healthcare - MedCity News
item.description: An NYU Stern report links private equity in healthcare to worse outcomes and higher bankruptcy risk, calling for reforms and stronger oversight.

item.title: The Saga of Utah’s Rx Refill Bot: A Bold Bet on AI &amp;amp; Researchers Who Cried Foul - MedCity News
item.description: Utah is piloting an AI system developed by Doctronic to autonomously handle routine prescription refills, aiming to reduce delays and boost medication adherence. But a report from Mindgard AI claiming that there are vulnerabilities in the company’s chatbot underscores the broader challenge regulators and developers face in ensuring healthcare AI systems remain safe and reliable in real-world use.

item.title: Why GI Providers Should Care About That “Health Hack” - MedCity News
item.description: Patients want to explore more holistic options and are becoming more educated and interested in their own health. However, this trend of growing trust in unchecked online health advice often introduces more risk to patients than help.

item.title: Imaging Interoperability Offers a Lifeline to Rural Hospitals and the Patients Depending on Them - MedCity News
item.description: Typically, rural hospitals operate as “islands,” where a patient might receive an initial scan at a community health facility, see a specialist at a regional medical center, and return home for follow-up care. In this scenario, it’s common for their medical images to become trapped in three different systems.

item.title: Why Novartis Is Paying $2B for a Cancer Drug That Hits the Same Target as One of Its Own Products - MedCity News
item.description: Novartis already markets the PI3Kα inhibitor Piqray for breast cancer, but acquiring a Synnovation Therapeutics subsidiary brings an early clinical program that the pharma company claims could be best in the class of next-generation therapies for the target. Competitors include Eli Lilly, Relay Therapeutics, and OnKure Therapeutics.

item.title: 12 Senate Democrats Unveil Plan to Cut Costs, Expand Coverage - MedCity News
item.description: In a recent letter, Senate Democrats proposed lowering healthcare costs, expanding coverage and cracking down on insurance company practices.

item.title: Why Pure DTC Doesn’t Work in Healthcare, Per Muse Capital - MedCity News
item.description: Rachel Springate, general partner at Muse Capital, said the next wave of healthcare startups will be driven by consumer demand — but pure direct-to-consumer models rarely work. Companies like Midi Health, Mavida Health and Mahmee are showing a different path: starting with patients, collecting outcomes data, and integrating with clinicians, payers and the broader healthcare system.

item.title: AI Won’t Replace Clinical Trial Teams, But It Fixes the Bottlenecks That Keep Patients Out - MedCity News
item.description: We don’t have a shortage of willing patients — instead we have a shortage of scalable ways to identify and engage them responsibly. AI, used meaningfully offers a reliable path forward.

item.title: Virtual Specialty Care Has Time. Will We Use It Wisely? - MedCity News
item.description: The specialty access and capacity crisis demands more than incremental fixes. It requires expanding virtual access and fundamentally rethinking how specialty care can be delivered.

item.title: Why Some Hospitals Are Betting on Midstream Health to Help Eliminate Waste - MedCity News
item.description: Midstream Health is taking a bit of a different approach to healthcare AI by focusing on reducing hospitals’ costs rather than boosting their revenue. The startup uses AI to identify savings opportunities across fragmented spending data, which helps health systems like Mount Sinai and CommonSpirit quickly improve their purchasing decisions.

item.title: Novartis Antimalarial Clears Key WHO Review to Get the Combo Drug to Babies - MedCity News
item.description: The World Health Organization has prequalified Coartem Baby, the first and only antimalarial for babies. Novartis developed this combination drug in partnership with Medicines for Malaria Venture.

item.title: AMA Calls on Congress to Improve Safeguards for AI Mental Health Chatbots - MedCity News
item.description: The American Medical Association is urging Congress to add safeguards for AI mental health chatbots amid safety concerns, while noting their potential to expand access.

item.title: Driving Outcomes with a Digital Transportation Infrastructure - MedCity News
item.description: Transportation is a vital part of the care journey, and if we are serious about improving outcomes, reducing missed appointments, and supporting healthier members, we have to be honest about where friction still exists and focus on removing it.

item.title: Healthcare’s Identity Crisis: Why A Single Prescription Requires Multiple Logins - MedCity News
item.description: Now is the time to solve the industry’s identity crisis, and it can only be done through a combination of phishing-resistant and adaptive MFA, fine-grained access control, and standards-based interoperability.
